facts.raw_span: A 28-year-old G2P1 woman presented 31 days after an elective cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia
with worsening headache and easy fatigability for 3 days
The headache was continuous, global, and had become severe over 24 hours
associated with nausea and malaise
Eight days postoperatively she had developed a mild global headache managed with rest and paracetamol
By day 31 the headache was severe, nonpositional, and unrelieved by rest or analgesics
Vital signs were normal
She was fully conscious and oriented
all meningeal signs were negative
motor function was intact
Laboratory studies showed a normal complete blood count, prothrombin time, partial prothrombin time, and international normalized ratio

Noncontrast CT of the head revealed a layered hypodense crescent-shaped extra-axial collection over the left frontoparietal convexity with areas of linear and crescentic hyperdensity, measuring 15 mm in width with a 13-mm midline shift

concepts.why: The patient presented with worsening headache and easy fatigability after an elective cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia, which is consistent with post-dural puncture headache.
The noncontrast CT of the head revealed a layered hypodense crescent-shaped extra-axial collection over the left frontoparietal convexity, which is consistent with subdural hematoma.
The patient presented with a severe, nonpositional headache that was unrelieved by rest or analgesics, which is consistent with migraine.
The patient presented with a mild global headache that was managed with rest and paracetamol, which is consistent with tension headache.
The patient presented with a continuous, global headache that had become severe over 24 hours, which is consistent with chronic daily headache.
The patient presented with a severe, nonpositional headache that was unrelieved by rest or analgesics, which is consistent with cervicogenic headache.

The noncontrast CT of the head revealed a layered hypodense crescent-shaped extra-axial collection over the left frontoparietal convexity, which is consistent with idiopathic intracranial hypertension.

rationales.F01: The patient's history of cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia increases the likelihood of post-dural puncture headache.
rationales.F05: The development of a mild global headache eight days postoperatively, managed with rest and paracetamol, is consistent with post-dural puncture headache.
rationales.F09: The absence of meningeal signs decreases the likelihood of subdural hematoma.
rationales.F12: The presence of a layered hypodense crescent-shaped extra-axial collection on noncontrast CT of the head is highly suggestive of subdural hematoma.
